source.original_text:
Attributed scoped mathematical restatement with explicit generalization:
E is a complete real inner-product space (a real Hilbert space), including dimension zero. f:E->R is globally C2 in the Frechet sense. x,y and every test vector range over all E.
alpha,beta are real and may be signed. For every z,v, alpha||v||^2 <= D2f(z)[v,v] <= beta||v||^2. These are bounds on the genuine nested Frechet derivative, not on an independently supplied operator.
H(x,y) is the ordinary Lebesgue Bochner integral on[0,1] of the Riesz-represented D2f(y+t(x-y)). Its symmetry, continuity/measurability/integrability and secant identity are conclusions derived from C2, not hypotheses. Completeness permits the Riesz identification and Bochner operator integral.
For every complete real inner-product space E, every globally C2 real f with signed global genuine-Hessian diagonal bounds alpha,beta, and all x,y, let phi(t) be the Riesz operator of D2f(y+t(x-y)) and H=integral_0^1 phi(t) dt in ordinary Lebesgue measure. Then phi is interval integrable, gradient f x-gradient f y=H(x-y), H is symmetric, all v satisfy alpha||v||^2<=inner(Hv,v)<=beta||v||^2, and ||H||op<=max(|alpha|,|beta|). In finite Euclidean space this specializes to the source actual H with alpha=1/(2kappa),beta=1; V_eta smoothness/curvature must still be proved separately.
Only the actual Hessian-segment constructor in Lemma4.6. The source smoothed-potential C2/curvature producer, actual Picard-node weighted average H, first-order endpoint expansion/operator remainder, deterministic K contraction, stochastic Khat/Kbar, repeated history, PBPS and both full main results/composition remain independent. The signed Hilbert generalization is background, not an extra assumption on the finite-dimensional source theorem. No probability/cost guarantee or implemented kernel is asserted here.

blind_reconstruction.text:
Let E be any complete real inner-product space with the induced norm; no finite-dimensionality assumption is imposed. Let f:E->R be globally twice continuously Frechet differentiable, and let alpha,beta be arbitrary real numbers. Suppose, for every z,v in E,
  alpha||v||^2 <= D^2 f(z)[v,v] <= beta||v||^2.
For every pair x,y in E define, for all real t,
  phi(t)=A(y+t(x-y)),
where A(z) is the actual continuous linear Riesz operator associated to the continuous bilinear form D^2 f(z), characterized by
  <A(z)v,w>=D^2 f(z)[v,w] for all v,w in E.
Define the continuous linear operator
  H=integral_0^1 phi(t) dt
as an ordinary Lebesgue Bochner interval integral taking values in the complete normed space of continuous real linear operators E->E. Then the following five conclusions hold simultaneously:
  phi is interval integrable with respect to real Lebesgue measure on 0..1;
  grad f(x)-grad f(y)=H(x-y);
  H is symmetric, meaning <Hv,w>=<v,Hw> for all v,w in E;
  alpha||v||^2 <= <Hv,v> <= beta||v||^2 for every v in E;
  ||H||_operator <= max(|alpha|,|beta|).
The gradient is the Riesz representative of the first Frechet derivative, and D^2 f(z) is the actual nested second Frechet derivative evaluated on its two vector arguments. The operator norm is the induced norm, not a matrix-entry norm.
The operator H is fixed by this integral along the segment from y to x, rather than chosen as an existential secant witness. Integrability, the exact gradient-secant identity, symmetry, quadratic-form bounds and the norm estimate are conclusions, not additional certificate assumptions. The theorem covers x=y and permits arbitrary signs of alpha,beta subject to the stated all-point/all-vector inequalities; it does not separately assume alpha>=0, beta>=0 or alpha<=beta. No probability law, finite basis, matrix, stochastic process or sampled mean-value point is supplied.

/-!
# Genuine Hessian segment integral

SPHMC arXiv:2609.06906v1 Lemma 4.6 uses the integral of the genuine Hessian
along a segment to represent a gradient difference. C² supplies symmetry and
continuous Bochner integrability. The complete real Hilbert-space statement
retains signed curvature bounds and includes the source's finite Euclidean case.
It does not construct the smoothed potential or prove the downstream kernel step.
-/

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.HessianSecantOperator

open Set InnerProductSpace MeasureTheory
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E]

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
/-- The actual Riesz Hessian segment integral is a symmetric gradient secant
operator with inherited signed curvature bounds and the endpoint norm bound.
No operator, gradient identity, symmetry or integrability certificate is assumed. -/
theorem hessian_secant_operator {f : E → ℝ} {α β : ℝ}
    (hf : ContDiff ℝ 2 f)
    (hlo : ∀ z v, α * ‖v‖ ^ 2 ≤ (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) z v) v)
    (hup : ∀ z v, (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) z v) v ≤ β * ‖v‖ ^ 2)
    (x y : E) :
    let φ := fun t : ℝ => continuousLinearMapOfBilin
      (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) (y + t • (x - y)))
    let H := ∫ t : ℝ in 0..1, φ t
    IntervalIntegrable φ volume 0 1 ∧
      gradient f x - gradient f y = H (x - y) ∧
      H.IsSymmetric ∧
      (∀ v, α * ‖v‖ ^ 2 ≤ inner ℝ (H v) v ∧
        inner ℝ (H v) v ≤ β * ‖v‖ ^ 2) ∧
      ‖H‖ ≤ max |α| |β| := by
  let φ := fun t : ℝ => continuousLinearMapOfBilin
    (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) (y + t • (x - y)))
  let H := ∫ t : ℝ in 0..1, φ t
  change IntervalIntegrable φ volume 0 1 ∧ _
  have hfd : ContDiff ℝ 1 (fderiv ℝ f) := hf.fderiv_right (by norm_num)
  have hc : Continuous φ := by
    unfold φ continuousLinearMapOfBilin
    exact continuous_const.clm_comp ((hfd.continuous_fderiv (by norm_num)).comp
      (continuous_const.add (continuous_id.smul continuous_const)))
  have hi : IntervalIntegrable φ volume 0 1 := hc.intervalIntegrable 0 1
  have hinner (v w : E) : inner ℝ (H v) w =
      ∫ t : ℝ in 0..1, (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) (y + t • (x - y)) v) w := by
    change inner ℝ ((∫ t : ℝ in 0..1, φ t) v) w = _
    rw [ContinuousLinearMap.intervalIntegral_apply hi v, real_inner_comm]
    change (innerSL ℝ w) (∫ t : ℝ in 0..1, φ t v) = _
    rw [← (innerSL ℝ w).intervalIntegral_comp_comm
      (((hc.clm_apply continuous_const : Continuous (fun t => φ t v))).intervalIntegrable
        (μ := volume) 0 1)]
    apply intervalIntegral.integral_congr
    intro t _
    exact (real_inner_comm w (φ t v)).symm.trans
      (continuousLinearMapOfBilin_apply _ v w)
  have hgrad : gradient f x - gradient f y = H (x - y) := by
    apply ext_inner_right ℝ
    intro w
    rw [hinner]
    have hd (t : ℝ) : HasDerivAt
        (fun s : ℝ => fderiv ℝ f (y + s • (x - y)) w)
        ((fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) (y + t • (x - y)) (x - y)) w) t := by
      convert ((hfd.differentiable_one _).hasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt t
        (((hasDerivAt_id t).smul_const (x - y)).const_add y)).clm_apply
        (hasDerivAt_const t w) using 1 <;> first | rfl | simp
    have hdcont : Continuous (fun t : ℝ =>
        (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) (y + t • (x - y)) (x - y)) w) :=
      (((hfd.continuous_fderiv (by norm_num)).comp
        (continuous_const.add (continuous_id.smul continuous_const))).clm_apply
          continuous_const).clm_apply continuous_const
    simpa [inner_sub_left, gradient, Function.comp_def] using
      (intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt
        (fun t _ => hd t) (hdcont.intervalIntegrable 0 1)).symm
  have hsym : H.IsSymmetric := by
    intro v w
    change inner ℝ (H v) w = inner ℝ v (H w)
    have hw : inner ℝ v (H w) =
        ∫ t : ℝ in 0..1, (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) (y + t • (x - y)) w) v :=
      (real_inner_comm v (H w)).symm.trans (hinner w v)
    rw [hinner, hw]
    apply intervalIntegral.integral_congr
    intro t _
    exact hf.contDiffAt.isSymmSndFDerivAt (by norm_num) v w
  have hbound (v : E) : α * ‖v‖ ^ 2 ≤ inner ℝ (H v) v ∧
      inner ℝ (H v) v ≤ β * ‖v‖ ^ 2 := by
    have hvcont : Continuous (fun t : ℝ =>
        (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) (y + t • (x - y)) v) v) :=
      (((hfd.continuous_fderiv (by norm_num)).comp
        (continuous_const.add (continuous_id.smul continuous_const))).clm_apply
          continuous_const).clm_apply continuous_const
    rw [hinner]
    constructor
    · simpa using intervalIntegral.integral_mono_on (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 1)
        (intervalIntegrable_const : IntervalIntegrable (fun _ : ℝ => α * ‖v‖ ^ 2) volume 0 1)
        (hvcont.intervalIntegrable 0 1) (fun t _ => hlo _ v)
    · simpa using intervalIntegral.integral_mono_on (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 1)
        (hvcont.intervalIntegrable 0 1)
        (intervalIntegrable_const : IntervalIntegrable (fun _ : ℝ => β * ‖v‖ ^ 2) volume 0 1)
        (fun t _ => hup _ v)
  refine ⟨hi, hgrad, hsym, hbound, ?_⟩
  rw [H.norm_eq_iSup_rayleighQuotient hsym]
  apply ciSup_le
  intro v
  change |inner ℝ (H v) v / ‖v‖ ^ 2| ≤ max |α| |β|
  by_cases hv : v = 0
  · simp [hv]
  · simp only [abs_div, abs_pow, abs_norm]
    apply (div_le_iff₀ (sq_pos_of_pos (norm_pos_iff.mpr hv))).mpr
    have hl := (hbound v).1
    have hu := (hbound v).2
    have hl' := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right
      ((neg_le_abs α).trans (le_max_left |α| |β|)) (sq_nonneg ‖v‖)
    have hu' := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right
      ((le_abs_self β).trans (le_max_right |α| |β|)) (sq_nonneg ‖v‖)
    exact abs_le.mpr ⟨by nlinarith, by nlinarith⟩

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.HessianSecantOperator

steps.title: Construct the actual operator and derive regularity
steps.text: Represent each genuine second derivative by the continuous Riesz map, using Mathlib continuousLinearMapOfBilin. C2 makes Df C1 and D2f continuous. Composing with the affine segment and fixed continuous Riesz map gives a continuous operator-valued phi; hence its ordinary unit-interval Bochner integral exists. No matrix or integrability certificate is supplied.

steps.title: Commute genuine integral evaluation and arbitrary pairing
steps.text: Continuous evaluation and the fixed continuous linear functional inner(w,.) commute with the actual Bochner integral. Real symmetry of the inner product turns this into the displayed all-vector identity. Both integral commutations use the derived interval integrability.

steps.title: Derive the full gradient secant identity by FTC
steps.text: Put v=x-y. For any w, differentiating t -> Df(y+t v)[w] gives D2f(y+t v)[v,w]. Its continuity supplies scalar integrability. The ordinary FTC gives the difference Df(x)[w]-Df(y)[w]; Riesz identifies it with inner(gradient f x-gradient f y,w). Equality against every w yields the full vector equality, not merely its diagonal pairing.
steps.lean: hgrad; hd; hdcont; integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt; gradient; ext_inner_right

steps.title: Inherit genuine symmetry
steps.text: C2 supplies symmetry of the actual second derivative. The all-vector pairing identity shows inner(Hv,w)=inner(Hw,v)=inner(v,Hw). This does not assume self-adjointness of an unrelated matrix.

steps.title: Integrate the actual two diagonal bounds
steps.text: For each v, integrate the constant bounds alpha||v||^2 and beta||v||^2 against ordinary Lebesgue measure on the unit interval. Integral monotonicity and hinner give the inherited inequalities. Signed moduli and dimension zero require no extra positivity or order hypothesis.

steps.title: Control the actual operator norm
steps.text: For the symmetric H, Mathlib identifies its norm with the supremum of absolute Rayleigh quotients. For nonzero v, the previous signed inequalities bound their absolute value by max(|alpha|,|beta|); v=0 gives zero. This proves the stated norm bound even on the zero space. In the paper alpha=1/(2kappa),beta=1,kappa>=1 gives norm<=1 once its curvature premises are produced.

lesson.lean_statement: Exact nested genuine Frechet derivative, Riesz operator and ordinary unit-interval Bochner integral; all-vector identity and signed bounds.
lesson.lean_proof: Continuous Riesz composition, operator/inner integral commutation, arbitrary-pairing FTC, genuine C2 symmetry, integral order and symmetric Rayleigh norm.
